subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The common masses __have waited__ for three hours to meet the king in the royal court.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"have been waiting"** indicates an action that started in the past and is still continuing up to the present moment. (प्रतीक्षा कर रहे हैं)

 
 
• **Example:** They **have been waiting** for the bus for over an hour now.
 
 
 
• **"Waited"** refers to an action that was completed in the past. (प्रतीक्षा की)
 
 
• **Example:** She** waited **for him at the café yesterday.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: had waiting** (प्रतीक्षा कर रहे थे): This is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "had been waiting".

 
 
• **Example:** They had been waiting for the train before it was canceled.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: will waiting** (प्रतीक्षा करेंगे): This is grammatically incorrect. The correct form should be "will be waiting".
 
 
• **Example:** She will be waiting for you at the station.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: has been waiting** (प्रतीक्षा कर रहा है): This is grammatically incorrect because "common masses" is plural and requires "have" instead of "has".
 
 
• **Example:** He has been waiting for his friend for two hours.
 
 

 

4a:Tb60,

The correct answer is: **Option 2)**
